name: The Tracker Sync
oneLiner: Refreshes the master QA status workbook from live ADO data — hours, bug counts, statuses — via Microsoft Graph download/upload, no manual data entry.
lead: Teams keep a master status workbook — one row per feature/story, with columns for logged hours, bugs, pass/fail tallies, and status. This agent pulls the file from SharePoint over Microsoft Graph, queries ADO for the live figures, writes every cell with `exceljs`, and PUTs the updated workbook back.
chore: Keeping that workbook current is a weekly grind. Someone opens ADO, looks up each story's QA hours, counts its bugs, tallies pass/fail, checks status, and types it into the right cell — every row, every sprint. It takes hours, the numbers are stale the moment they're typed, and a fat-fingered figure quietly misleads everyone reading the report.
instead: The agent downloads the workbook from SharePoint, then per story queries ADO for the real figures — logged QA hours (`CompletedWork`), child bug count, pass/fail, and `System.State` — and writes them into the current sprint's columns. It rebuilds a severity-color-coded bug sheet, refreshes each story's status, then uploads the file back. A `--dry-run` mode writes locally without publishing.
whyItMatters: A status report that's automatically accurate means leadership decides on live numbers, not a workbook that quietly drifted out of date.

howItWorks.step: It resolves the current sprint (or the one you name) and downloads the master workbook from SharePoint over Microsoft Graph.
howItWorks.explain: The whole function is guarded by a graceful degradation contract: a missing `GRAPH_TOKEN` returns `null` (not an error), which is the caller's signal to fall back to a local copy instead of failing the run. The Graph URL is the fiddly part — the SharePoint path is `encodeURIComponent`'d to escape spaces and special characters, but then `%2F` is un-escaped back to `/` because the drive addressing syntax `root:/path/to/file:/content` needs **real slashes** as path separators while everything else stays encoded. Success is narrowed to `status === 200` **and** a present `result.buffer` — a 200 with no body still returns `null` rather than a truthy-but-empty download, so the caller never syncs into an empty workbook.

howItWorks.step: For each story, it queries ADO for logged QA hours and writes them into that sprint's columns.
howItWorks.explain: Logged QA effort lives on the story's child Tasks, not the story, so this walks `Hierarchy-Forward` (parent → child) relations and extracts each child's ID from `r.url` with the regex `/workItems\/(\d+)/` — ADO relations carry the target only inside the URL. It **sums** `Microsoft.VSTS.Scheduling.CompletedWork` (ADO's field for hours actually logged, as opposed to `RemainingWork`) across only Tasks whose lowercased title contains `qa_test`, so non-QA child tasks under the same story don't inflate the figure. Every read is defensive: no children short-circuits to `0`, and `|| 0` covers a Task that exists but has never had hours logged, so a story mid-flight reports real partial hours rather than `NaN`.

howItWorks.step: It also queries ADO for each story's child bug count and writes it into the same row.
howItWorks.explain: The same `Hierarchy-Forward` walk as the hours query, but the payoff is a count: after batch-fetching the children it filters to `System.WorkItemType === 'Bug'` and returns `.length`. It requests `System.State` in the batch even though the count ignores it — the field is fetched so the shared batch shape matches the bug-sheet rebuild elsewhere, avoiding a second round-trip. This counts **every** child bug regardless of state, so a closed/fixed bug still contributes to the story's total defect count — the number reflects bugs *found*, not bugs *open*.

howItWorks.step: It refreshes each story's `System.State` (New, Active, Resolved, Closed) and color-codes the cell so state reads at a glance.
howItWorks.explain: This writes the story's live `System.State` into the workbook and colors it so the state reads at a glance. `row.getCell(5)` is column 5 (1-indexed in `exceljs`, not 0-indexed) — the status column — and the value is set before the color so a state always lands even if it matches no branch. Colors are `exceljs` **ARGB** strings, where the leading `FF` is the alpha (fully opaque) followed by the RGB hex — omit the alpha and the color silently won't apply. The `if` guard skips the whole write when `state` is empty, so a story ADO returned nothing for keeps its previous cell rather than being blanked; and only the three known states (`Closed`/`Active`/`New`) get recolored — any other state writes the text but leaves the font as-is, so the value is never hidden just because it wasn't anticipated.

howItWorks.step: It writes a local backup, then PUTs the finished workbook back to SharePoint.
howItWorks.explain: The mirror of the download: a **PUT** of the raw bytes to the same `root:/path:/content` endpoint, which **overwrites** the existing file in place (Graph's simple upload — fine here because the workbook is small; files over ~4 MB would need a chunked upload session instead). The same `encodeURIComponent` → restore-`%2F` path dance is repeated so upload and download address the identical file. A missing token returns `false` up front rather than attempting an unauthenticated write, and success is any **2xx** (`>= 200 && < 300`) — not just 200 — because Graph may answer a create-or-replace with `201 Created` the first time and `200 OK` thereafter.

examples.input: Sync this sprint's numbers into the master QA tracker.
examples.output: Downloaded the workbook, updated 18 story rows with hours and bug counts, refreshed 40 statuses, rebuilt the bug sheet (23 bugs), and PUT the file back. 0 errors.

underHood.heading: Downloading the workbook
underHood.whenRuns: First, unless you point it at a local file.
underHood.input: A SharePoint file path and a Microsoft Graph token.
underHood.output: The master workbook downloaded into a Buffer, plus a local backup copy.

underHood.heading: Querying ADO for live figures
underHood.whenRuns: Once per story row in the sprint being synced.
underHood.output: Its total logged QA hours (summed `CompletedWork` across the qa_test Tasks) and its child bug count.

underHood.heading: Refreshing story status
underHood.whenRuns: For every row in the Feature Summary sheet.
underHood.output: The status cell updated with color-coded font — green (Closed), blue (Active), gray (New).

underHood.heading: Rebuilding the bug sheet
underHood.whenRuns: After the story rows are updated.
underHood.input: Every bug found under every story, across all features.
underHood.output: A sorted, severity-color-coded bug table on its own sheet.

underHood.heading: Publishing the workbook
underHood.whenRuns: Last, unless it's a dry run or local-only pass.
underHood.input: The updated workbook, written locally first.
underHood.output: The file PUT back to SharePoint over Microsoft Graph, ready for the team to open.

prerequisites: Node ≥ 18 and a terminal (macOS/Linux shell or Windows PowerShell).
Azure DevOps access with a **PAT**, and SharePoint access with a **Microsoft Graph token** (needed only for the download/upload steps).
The master status workbook already on SharePoint, in the format this agent expects — a 'Sprint Tracker' sheet and a 'Feature Summary' sheet.

steps.label: Install Node.js — the engine that runs the agent.
steps.cmd:
# macOS (with Homebrew):
brew install node

# or download the LTS installer from nodejs.org, then check it worked:
node -v   # should print v18 or higher
steps.why: The agent is TypeScript run under Node — a one-time per-machine install.

steps.label: Clone the agent and install its dependencies.
steps.why: `npm install` pulls `exceljs` and the ADO/Graph clients into `node_modules`.
steps.firstRun: Cold install — a minute or two.

steps.label: Set the ADO and Graph credentials (env vars).
steps.cmd:
export ADO_ORGANIZATION=my-org
export ADO_PROJECT="My Project"
export ADO_PAT=your-access-token
export GRAPH_API_TOKEN=your-graph-token   # only needed to download/upload
steps.why: The PAT reads live hours/bugs/status from ADO; the Graph token fetches and publishes the workbook. Without the Graph token it falls back to a local copy of the file.

steps.label: Preview a sync with --dry-run.
steps.why: `--dry-run` mode: downloads the current workbook, pulls the live figures from ADO, and writes a local copy — but skips the upload, so nothing on SharePoint changes yet.
steps.firstRun: Pulls the full workbook plus every story's figures for the chosen sprint.
steps.rerun: Safe to repeat — it re-reads the latest figures each time.

steps.label: Run the real sync and publish it.
steps.why: Same steps as the dry run, but PUTs the finished workbook back to SharePoint so the rest of the team sees the refreshed numbers.
steps.rerun: Idempotent — recomputes every cell from live ADO data and overwrites the previous version, so re-running (e.g. weekly) just keeps the sheet current.

steps.label: Open the local backup, if you just want to look.
steps.why: A local backup is always written before any upload, so you can inspect exactly what went out — or work fully offline with `--local-only`.

inputs.name: --sprint <name>
inputs.desc: Which sprint's columns to refresh (defaults to whichever sprint's dates cover today).

inputs.name: --dry-run
inputs.desc: Sync from ADO but skip the SharePoint upload.

inputs.name: --local-only / --file <path>
inputs.desc: Skip SharePoint entirely and read/write a local (or manually downloaded) copy.

inputs.name: --download-only
inputs.desc: Just fetch the current workbook from SharePoint; don't sync or upload.

outputs.name: Q3_QA_Tracker.xlsx (local backup)
outputs.desc: Written before every run, with the sprint's hours/bugs and every story's status refreshed.

outputs.name: the same file, republished
outputs.desc: PUT back to SharePoint so the whole team sees the current numbers (unless --dry-run or --local-only).

outputs.name: rebuilt Bug Summary sheet
outputs.desc: Every bug under every story, sorted and color-coded by severity and state.

runbook.rerun: Idempotent by design — every pass recomputes each cell from live ADO data and overwrites what was there, so running it weekly (or on a schedule) is exactly the intended use; no accumulating state goes stale.
runbook.integrate: Schedule the real sync (not the dry run) to run at the start of each week so the status workbook leadership reads from is never more than a few days stale.

video.caption: A 3-minute screen recording: preview a sync, then publish the refreshed status workbook.
script: Open a terminal beside the current status spreadsheet.
Say: 'Keeping this sheet current used to be a weekly grind. Watch this instead.'
Run `node -v` and `npm install` (or note it's already done).
Show the `export ADO_...` and `GRAPH_API_TOKEN` lines — the only project-specific part.
Run `npm run qa:tracker:sync -- --sprint S10`; narrate the per-row hours/bugs it prints as it queries the board.
Open the local backup file it produced; show one row's hours and bug count updated.
Run the real sync (no --dry-run); note the 'Uploading to SharePoint... done' line.
Switch to the shared drive in a browser and refresh — show the live file now matches.
Point out the rebuilt Bug Summary sheet, color-coded by severity.
Close: 'Same command, safe to run every week — it just recomputes and republishes.'
